content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Primary PFS estimand lacks explicit intercurrent event strategy for death",
      "quote": "PFS is censored at the date of last evaluable assessment before or on start of new anti-cancer therapy.",
      "page": 48,
      "section": "3 Objectives and Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The primary estimand for PFS only specifies censoring for start of new anti-cancer therapy, but does not explicitly address other intercurrent events such as death (which is part of the event) or treatment discontinuation for other reasons. The estimand framework should specify strategies for all relevant intercurrent events.",
      "fix": "Add explicit intercurrent event strategies for death (as event) and other treatment discontinuations (e.g., treatment policy or while-on-treatment strategy) in the primary estimand description."
    },
    {
      "title": "Secondary estimand for PRO lacks summary measure details",
      "quote": "Change from baseline to Week 12 in PRO endpoints between AMG 510 and docetaxel",
      "page": 48,
      "section": "3 Objectives and Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The PRO estimand states 'Change from baseline to Week 12' but does not specify the summary measure (e.g., mean change, difference in means, mixed model repeated measures estimate). This is a missing estimand attribute.",
      "fix": "Specify the summary measure for the PRO estimand, e.g., difference in least squares means from a mixed model for repeated measures."
    },
    {
      "title": "No analysis stated for DOR, TTR, and DCR endpoints",
      "quote": "To compare efficacy of AMG 510 versus docetaxel as assessed by: duration of response (DOR), time to response (TTR), and disease control rate (DCR)",
      "page": 48,
      "section": "3 Objectives and Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The objectives list DOR, TTR, and DCR as secondary endpoints, but the extracted facts show no analysis IDs (ana_*) linked to these endpoints. The protocol text does not provide any statistical analysis methods for these endpoints, leaving a gap.",
      "fix": "Add a statistical analysis section describing the analysis methods for DOR (e.g., Kaplan-Meier and Cox model), TTR (e.g., cumulative incidence), and DCR (e.g., logistic regression)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing analysis for safety endpoint",
      "quote": "To compare the safety and tolerability of AMG 510 versus docetaxel",
      "page": 48,
      "section": "3 Objectives and Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The safety objective is listed but no corresponding endpoint or analysis is described in the extracted text. The protocol should specify safety endpoints (e.g., adverse events, laboratory abnormalities) and their analysis methods.",
      "fix": "Add a safety endpoint definition and statistical analysis plan (e.g., descriptive statistics, incidence rates, and comparison of treatment-emergent adverse events)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing analysis for PK endpoint",
      "quote": "To characterize the pharmacokinetics (PK) of AMG 510 and its major metabolites",
      "page": 48,
      "section": "3 Objectives and Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The PK objective is listed but no PK endpoints or analysis methods are described in the extracted text. The protocol should specify PK parameters (e.g., AUC, Cmax) and their analysis.",
      "fix": "Add PK endpoint definitions and analysis methods (e.g., non-compartmental analysis, descriptive statistics)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent definition of PFS between primary endpoint and estimand",
      "quote": "Progression will be based on an independent radiologic assessment of disease response per RECIST v1.1.",
      "page": 38,
      "section": "2.1.2 Primary Endpoints",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The primary endpoint definition says 'independent radiologic assessment' but the objectives table says 'blinded independent central review (BICR)'. These may be the same, but the wording is inconsistent and could lead to ambiguity.",
      "fix": "Use consistent terminology, e.g., 'blinded independent central review (BICR)' throughout the protocol."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing sample size inputs for secondary endpoints",
      "quote": "The primary endpoint of Study 20190009 is progression-free Survival (PFS).",
      "page": 38,
      "section": "2.1.2 Primary Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The extracted text does not include any sample size section or inputs (e.g., assumed hazard ratio, alpha, power, dropout rate). Without this, the sample size justification is missing, which is a critical gap for the statistical section.",
      "fix": "Add a sample size section with all inputs: assumed PFS hazard ratio, median PFS, alpha, power, randomization ratio, and dropout rate."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing multiplicity adjustment for multiple secondary endpoints",
      "quote": "The key secondary endpoints are OS, objective response rate (ORR), patient-reported outcomes (PRO), including change from baseline (cycle 1 day 1) over time to week 12 in disease related symptoms (dyspnea, cough, and chest pain), physical functioning, and health related quality of life (QOL).",
      "page": 38,
      "section": "2.1.3 Key Secondary Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol lists multiple key secondary endpoints but does not describe any multiplicity control strategy (e.g., hierarchical testing, alpha allocation). This is a common regulatory requirement and a missing analysis gap.",
      "fix": "Add a section on multiplicity adjustment for key secondary endpoints, e.g., a hierarchical testing procedure or graphical approach."
    }
  ]
}
